notes: Sources: archive.org scans of BYTE, Kilobaud, Creative Computing, Personal Computing and COMPUTE! (full text searched for Jobs mentions), vintageapple.org scans (Softalk, Macworld Apr 1984, PC World), Computer History Museum 'This Day in History', Time (Feb 15 1982, Jan 3 1983), the Steve Jobs Archive (stevejobsarchive.com and book.stevejobsarchive.com), and Wikipedia. Nothing is from memory; every cell text comes from a page I opened. Thin areas: 1955-1971 (almost no month-level evidence; year-only items are marked to-confirm with placeholder months, e.g. Patty 1957, Mountain View 1959, Los Altos 1967, HP job 1968, Homestead 1968/1972) and 1973-1975 (Atari, India, Breakout have only a year or season). NYT archive pages (nytimes.com) and web.archive.org could not be fetched, tech-insider.org (NYT mirror) returned 410, folklore.org and Stanford's Macintosh site were unreachable, and Isaacson/Google Books pages show no text, so Apple events after 1980 lean on magazine scans and Wikipedia. The WebSearch budget ran out partway through, so some months may have verifiable items I did not find. Weak cells: several 'In the news' items are brief mentions (1980-11 COMPUTE! timeline, 1983-08 Apple Cart column, 1983-11 PC World interview, 1983-07 Creative Computing, 1984-11 and 1984-12) kept only for dated coverage. 1981-03 (chairman) relies on a search-result snippet of a NYT item mirrored at tech-insider.org (page itself not opened) plus Softalk Jun 1981, which confirms Jobs took Markkula's chairman seat but gives no month. 1982-05 AppleFest '82 rests on Softalk Apr 1982 (keynote planned for May) and Softalk Jul 1982 (Jobs and Woz spoke at the Boston show). 1984-04 date (24 Apr) comes from Softalk Jun 1984, which names Jobs among the speakers. 1981-01 is Burrell Smith's 'around January 1981' (Macworld Apr 1984) and matches Wikipedia's History of Apple (Jan 1981). 1975-03 is Wozniak's first Homebrew meeting (5 Mar 1975); Jobs's own attendance has no month. Sources for the Byte Shop order and the Apple I Homebrew demo conflict (April vs July 1976; Creative Computing says spring), so no cell. Existing cells: Born, Reed, back in parents' house, Apple founded, Apple II shown, Lisa born, IPO and Macintosh are confirmed; 'Joins Atari' and the Hewlett job moved off placeholder months (see removed); India stays at 1974-06 (Wikipedia: mid-1974, about seven months); San Remo purchase kept at 1982 (year only). Percent_confirmed is confirmed cells divided by the 359 months. Locations: Los Gatos is new (Time 1983); India stay months are approximate; Palo Alto 1994 and the Woodside, Cupertino and Mountain View start months are unverified; no stay was recorded for the Oregon commune (All One Farm) because no dates were found.
